title: Scaling Agentic Capabilities via Grounded Interaction Synthesis

problem.claim: Agentic intelligence requires high-quality interaction data for completing complex tasks with diverse real-world tools.

gap.claim: LLM-only environment and task generation can produce biased sampling that lacks real-world diversity, difficulty, and high-fidelity long-horizon tasks.

contributions.claim: The work presents GAIS, a framework for scalable construction of diverse environments and complex tasks through two-phase grounding.
GAIS constructs protocol-anchored environments from real-world MCP servers and uses structure-guided planning with logical dependencies and adversarial policies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On BFCL, ?2-Bench, and ACEBench, GAIS-synthesized data reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and enables base models to match or surpass official instruction-tuned counterparts.
GAIS reportedly achieves higher data efficiency and scalability, with strong capabilities from less data and continued growth where baselines stagnate.

narrative_sequence.summary: Complex tool use depends on high-quality interaction data.
Existing LLM-only synthesis is costly to constrain and may fail to represent real-world diversity, difficulty, and long-horizon structure.
GAIS grounds environments in MCP servers and plans tasks with structural dependencies and adversarial policies.
The authors report benchmark gains, improved data efficiency, and continued scaling.

source_observation.claim: Protocol-anchored environments are derived from real-world MCP servers to support functional diversity and difficulty.

interpretation.claim: Anchoring synthesis to external tool protocols may reduce reliance on unconstrained model priors.

application.claim: When generating agent tasks, ground environments in executable or protocol-defined tool interfaces.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this grounding transfers to domains without MCP servers or how much manual curation is required.

source_observation.claim: Structure-guided planning enforces logical dependencies and adversarial policies during task generation.

interpretation.claim: Explicit structural constraints may help produce more complex and long-horizon tasks than unconstrained sampling.

application.claim: Use dependency-aware planning and adversarial constraints when synthesizing multi-step agent tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the planning algorithm, constraint coverage, or failure modes.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative result values or dataset sizes.
The abstract does not describe ablations, implementation details, or independent verification.
The abstract does not clarify the identity of ?2-Bench.
